LESSON: NULLIFIERS OF SAUM

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.4.1: Nullifiers of Saum

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Nullifiers of Saum. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should Muslims observe rules and regulation when fasting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum
2. practise saum as a pillar of Islam
3. appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety)

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: NULLIFIERS OF SAUM
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Nullifiers of Saum helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: NULLIFIERS OF SAUM
Study Nullifiers of Saum like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Nullifiers of Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Practise saum as a pillar of Islam

What this means
In this part you learn to practise saum as a pillar of Islam. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise saum as a pillar of Islam.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Nullifiers of Saum in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise saum as a pillar of Islam. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety)

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety). You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety).
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety). Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Nullifiers of Saum is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Nullifiers of Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Nullifiers of Saum in your own words. (skill: practise saum as a pillar of Islam)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety))

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Nullifiers of Saum to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum.
3. Practise this skill: practise saum as a pillar of Islam.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety).
5. Make one local Kenya example of Nullifiers of Saum from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Nullifiers of Saum: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Nullifiers of Saum?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should Muslims observe rules and regulation when fasting?
2. What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Nullifiers of Saum means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum.
5. Be able to: practise saum as a pillar of Islam.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
